title: Accabonac
summary: Accabonac is a placename in East Hampton associated with Accabonac Harbor, Springs, and nearby meadows adjoining Gardiner's Bay. Recorded forms include Acabonack and Acabonuk, and early records often apply the name to the meadows.
address_label: Accabonac Harbor / Springs, East Hampton, NY
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Montaukett Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: Accabonac preserves an Indigenous geographic description of East Hampton's estuarine landscape, with records connecting the name to a place where edible ground-nuts grow. Its many recorded spellings show how Native language, local ecology, and colonial paperwork intersect, often imperfectly, in the written record. The name keeps Long Island visible as a Native homeland shaped by land, water, plant knowledge, and continuing community memory.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Acabonack, Acabonuk, Occabonack, Accobannocke, Accaboneck, Occobonak, Ackobonuk, Ackabomtk, and Accaponack. The name is interpreted as a root place, while noting comparative linguistic evidence that remains tentative.

Why Place Names Matter

“Names are never neutral; they have something to teach us about our history and how we see ourselves in a place. They create a relationship.”

— Patty Krawec, Becoming Kin: An Indigenous Call to Unforgetting the Past and Reimagining Our Future (2022), Chapter 3, page 127
whereintheworld_content: Accabonac keeps a familiar East Hampton harbor name connected to Indigenous language, meadow use, and Montaukett place history. The history also shows why older translations should be preserved with caution: the early records are valuable, while the meaning still needs careful review.
